column1: Students who want to enter the University of Montreal’s Athletic Complex need more than just a conventional ID card – their identities must be authenticated by an electronic hand scanner.
column2: 想要进入蒙特利尔大学体育中心的学生，不仅需要普通的身份证，还必须通过电子手扫描仪验证身份。

column1: In some California housing estates, a key alone is insufficient to get someone in the door; his or her voiceprint must also be verified.
column2: 在加利福尼亚州的一些住宅区，仅凭一把钥匙是无法进入房屋的；还必须验证持证人的声音特征。

column1: And soon, customers at some Japanese banks will have to present their faces for scanning before they can enter the building and withdraw their money.
column2: 很快，一些日本银行的客户在进入银行并提取现金之前，必须进行面部识别扫描。

column1: All of these are applications of biometrics, a little-known but fast-growing technology that involves the use of physical or biological characteristics to identify individuals.
column2: 所有这些都属于生物识别技术的应用。生物识别技术是一种虽不太为人所知但发展迅速的技术，它利用人体或生物特征来进行身份识别。

column1: In use for more than a decade at some high-security government institutions in the United States and Canada, biometrics are now rapidly popping up in the everyday world.
column2: 在美加一些高安全级别的政府机构中，生物识别技术已使用超过十年，如今正迅速进入日常生活的各个领域。

column1: Already, more than 10,000 facilities, from prisons to day-care centres, monitor people’s fingerprints or other physical parts to ensure that they are who they claim to be.
column2: 目前，已有超过10,000个场所使用指纹或其他生物特征来验证人员身份，涵盖从监狱到托儿中心的各类设施，以此确保人们确实是他们自称的个体。

column1: Some 60 biometric companies around the world pulled in at least $22 million last year and that grand total is expected to mushroom to at least $50 million by 1999.
column2: 全球约有60家生物识别公司去年筹集了至少2200万美元，预计到1999年，这一总额将增至至少5000万美元。

column1: Biometric security systems operate by storing a digitised record of some unique human feature.
column2: 生物识别安全系统通过存储某种独特人体特征的数字化记录来运行。

column1: When an authorised user wishes to enter or use the facility, the system scans the person’s corresponding characteristics and attempts to match them against those on record.
column2: 当授权用户希望进入或使用设施时，系统会扫描该用户的相应特征，并尝试将其与记录中的信息进行比对。

column1: Systems using fingerprints, hands, voices, irises, retinas and faces are already on the market.
column2: 使用指纹、手掌、声音、虹膜、视网膜和面部识别的系统已经上市。

column1: Others using typing patterns and even body odours are in various stages of development.
column2: 采用打字模式甚至体味进行身份识别的技术，目前仍处于不同发展阶段。

column1: Fingerprint scanners are currently the most widely deployed type of biometric application, thanks to their growing use over the last 20 years by law-enforcement agencies.
column2: 指纹扫描仪目前是应用最广泛的生物识别技术，得益于执法机构过去20年来的广泛使用。

column1: Sixteen American states now use biometric fingerprint verification systems to check that people claiming welfare payments are genuine.
column2: 目前，美国有十六个州采用生物识别指纹验证系统，以核实声称领取福利的人确实是真实存在的。

column1: In June, politicians in Toronto voted to do the same, with a pilot project beginning next year.
column2: 六月份，多伦多的政界人士投票决定实施同样的计划，一个试点项目将于明年启动。

column1: To date, the most widely used commercial biometric system is the handkey, a type of hand scanner which reads the unique shape, size and irregularities of people’s hands.
column2: 迄今为止，最广泛使用的商业生物识别系统是手型识别技术，该技术通过读取人们手部的独特形状、尺寸和细微特征来实现识别功能。

column1: Originally developed for nuclear power plants, the handkey received its big break when it was used to control access to the Olympic Village in Atlanta by more than 65,000 athletes, trainers and support staff.
column2: 这种智能钥匙最初是为核电站开发的。后来，它在管理亚特兰大奥运会村的通行权限时发挥了重要作用——当时有超过65,000名运动员、教练以及工作人员使用这种钥匙来进出奥运村。从此，这种智能钥匙便声名鹊起。

column1: Now there are scores of other applications.
column2: 现在已有数十种其他应用。

column1: Around the world, the market is growing rapidly.
column2: 在全球范围内，这个市场的规模正在迅速扩张。

column1: Malaysia, for example, is preparing to equip all of its airports with biometric face scanners to match passengers with luggage.
column2: 例如，马来西亚正准备为所有机场配备生物识别面部扫描仪，以匹配乘客与行李。

column1: And Japan’s largest maker of cash dispensers is developing new machines that incorporate iris scanners.
column2: 而日本最大的自动取款机制造商正在研发新的机器，这些机器配备了虹膜扫描仪。

column1: The first commercial biometric, a hand reader used by an American firm to monitor employee attendance, was introduced in 1974.
column2: 第一种商业化的生物识别技术是一种手部识别器，由一家美国公司开发，用于监控员工的出勤情况，该产品于1974年推出。

column1: But only in the past few years has the technology improved enough for the prices to drop sufficiently to make them commercially viable.
column2: 不过，直到最近几年，技术才取得足够进步，使价格下降到足以实现商业可行性的程度。

column1: ‘When we started four years ago, I had to explain to everyone what a biometric is,’ says one marketing expert.
column2: ‘当四年前我们启动这项业务时，我不得不向每个人解释什么是生物识别技术，’一位营销专家表示。

column1: ‘Now, there’s much more awareness out there.’
column2: ‘现在，人们对这一问题的意识水平明显提高了。’

column1: Not surprisingly, biometrics raise thorny questions about privacy and the potential for abuse.
column2: 不出所料，生物识别技术引发了关于隐私和滥用风险的棘手问题。

column1: Some worry that governments and industry will be tempted to use the technology to monitor individual behaviour.
column2: 有些人担心，政府和相关行业可能会利用这项技术来监控个人的行为。

column1: ‘If someone used your fingerprints to match your health-insurance records with a credit-card record showing you regularly bought lots of cigarettes and fatty foods,’ says one policy analyst, ‘you would see your insurance payments go through the roof.’
column2: “如果有人用你的指纹来匹配你的医疗保险记录与信用卡信息，结果发现你经常购买大量香烟和高脂肪食品，”一位政策分析师说道，“那么你的保险费用就会变得非常高。”

column1: In Toronto, critics of the welfare fingerprint plan complained that it would stigmatise recipients by forcing them to submit to a procedure widely identified with criminals.
column2: 在多伦多，反对福利指纹计划的人抱怨说，该计划会通过强制受助者接受一个通常与罪犯关联的程序，使他们遭受污名化。

column1: Nonetheless, support for biometrics is growing in Toronto as it is in many other communities.
column2: 不过，多伦多及其他许多社区对生物识别技术的支持正在不断增长。

column1: In an increasingly crowded and complicated world, biometrics may well be a technology whose time has come.
column2: 在一个日益拥挤且复杂的世界上，生物识别技术或许正是其应运而生的时机。
